summary: John R. Brinkley, an American diploma-mill doctor, grew rich in the 1920s and 1930s implanting goat testicles into patients and selling remedies over his Kansas and Mexican border radio stations, maiming and killing many.

evidence.note: birth in 1885 and North Carolina childhood
first goat testicle implant on a Milford farmer after his 1917 army stint
buys an MD from an unaccredited Kansas City school in 1915
Los Angeles trip, implants for an LA Times editor and movie stars
builds KFKB radio station in Milford
radio station hires country musicians, helping spread the genre
Medical Question Box: diagnoses by radio, sells numbered drugs
write-in run for Kansas governor after licence revoked
moves to Del Rio, builds station on the Mexican side of the border
admires Hitler, hosts Coughlin and Kuhn, funds the Silver Shirts
Mexico shuts border stations in 1941; dies nearly broke in 1942

notes: Fascist sympathies get only a few minutes late in part 2, so fascism-far-right is borderline. Short trips to China and Japan left out of setting. The closing legacy remarks on country music and radio medicine are brief, so reaches_present is false. No QIDs given, not certain of them.
